title: Lesson 3 — Alphabetic Principle and Ehri’s Phases
source: User-supplied WGU D669 Lesson 3 Alphabetic Principle section
definition: The alphabetic principle is understanding that letters and letter patterns (graphemes) represent sounds (phonemes) in spoken language.
four_parts: Speech can be translated into written code (encoding)
Written code can be translated into speech (decoding)

ehri_phases.label: Pre-Alphabetic
features: Recognizes incidental visual features of words

ehri_phases.label: Partial Alphabetic
features: Early phonological and phonemic awareness: syllables, onset-rime, initial sound matching

ehri_phases.label: Full Alphabetic
features: Basic phonemic awareness: segmenting and blending 3–4 phonemes

ehri_phases.label: Consolidated Alphabetic
features: Uses orthographic mapping, word families, syllables, morphemes
Advanced phonemic awareness: deletion, substitution, phoneme reversal

grade_note: Grade markers reflect the supplied WGU figure's approximations, not universal developmental deadlines; instruction and individual student progress vary.
study_distinctions: Print awareness: understands meaning and organization of print
Alphabetic principle: knows graphemes represent phonemes
Decoding: transforms written word representations into spoken words
Encoding: transforms speech sounds into written representations
Phonics instruction explicitly teaches how spellings correspond to speech sounds

guided_practice.prompt: Which statement best describes the alphabetic principle?

options.text: It is the understanding of the meaning of words in a text.
It is the understanding that letters and letter patterns represent the sounds of spoken language.
It is the ability to read quickly and with expression.
It is the ability to recognize and name all the letters of the alphabet.

guided_practice.feedback_correct: The alphabetic principle refers to understanding how letters and letter combinations correspond to sounds in spoken language.

reflection_questions: Why do students need a firm understanding of the alphabetic principle?
What alphabetic-principle-related skills do students learn across K–3?
What are examples of pre-alphabetic word recognition?
Why does mastery of the alphabetic principle matter for phonics, fluency, and comprehension?
